body:
Hey Schema.org team,

I would like to propose two new schema types to better represent online prize competition / raffle platforms and the individual competitions they publish.

**Background**

There is currently no dedicated Schema.org type that accurately models online competition or raffle websites where users purchase entries/tickets for a chance to win a prize.

At present, many sites use Product schema to represent competitions because it is the closest available option. However, this creates semantic inaccuracies because:

- The item being offered is not the prize itself, it is simply the chance to win the item. Therefore the user is not purchasing ownership of a product, so product schema is incredibly misleading for this industry.
- The transaction represents entry into a competition/chance-based event. This is different to event schema in the sense that the event is continuously on-going. The deadline isn't the day of the event itself. 
- inventory, shipping, GTINs, brand ownership, and other Product concepts are often irrelevant or misleading for competitions/raffles.
- Search engines may incorrectly interpret the page as ecommerce product inventory.

This creates structured data ambiguity for both publishers and consumers of Schema.org data.


**Proposed Types**

- CompetitionBusiness (A subtype intended for businesses whose primary activity is operating online competitions, raffles, sweepstakes, or prize draws.)
- Competition or Raffle (A type representing an individual prize competition, raffle, sweepstake, or prize draw listing.)


**Suggested properties for Competition**

name
description
image
url
entryPrice
entryMethod
maximumEntries
closingDate
drawDate
winner
numberOfWinners
competitionStatus
eligibilityRequirement
minimumAge
organizer
oddsOfWinning
jurisdiction
termsAndConditions
hasPart
isAccessibleForFree


**Potential Benefits**
Competition businesses are growing rapidly in the UK, the EU and soon in the US. I believe there is a huge missed opportunity here and as someone who works in SEO within this industry, there are so many challenges when it comes to schema. 

Some of the potential benefits I can see these schema types benefitting. 

- More accurate semantic representation
- Reduced misuse of Product
- Improved search engine understanding
- Better structured data consistency across competition websites
- Clearer distinction between ecommerce and competition entry models
- Extensible support for regulated jurisdictions and compliance metadata


Thank you for considering the proposal!
title: Proposal: Add CompetitionBusiness and Competition types for prize competition / raffle websites

## Summary

`kaggle competitions list` does not show the authenticated user's competition rank, even though the API already returns it. Users who want their rank today have to download the full leaderboard and search locally (see #66).

This proposes exposing the existing `userRank` field in `competitions list` output.

## Current behavior

```bash
kaggle competitions list -g entered -v
```

```text
ref,deadline,category,reward,teamCount,userHasEntered
https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/example-comp,2026-08-01 00:00:00,Playground,Swag,1200,True
```

`userHasEntered` is shown, but rank is not, even when the user has a public leaderboard position.

The leaderboard commands (`competitions leaderboard --show` / `--download`) return `teamId`, `teamName`, `submissionDate`, and `score`. They do not include a rank column.

## What the API already provides

`competitions list` calls `ListCompetitions` via kagglesdk. The response uses `ApiCompetition`, which includes `userHasEntered` (already in CLI output) and `userRank` (returned by the API but not shown).

In `src/kaggle/api/kaggle_api_extended.py`, `competition_fields` omits `userRank`:

```python
competition_fields = ["ref", "deadline", "category", "reward", "teamCount", "userHasEntered"]
```

## Proposed change

Add `userRank` to `competition_fields` so it appears in table, CSV (`-v`), and `--format` output.

```bash
kaggle competitions list -g entered -v
```

```text
ref,deadline,category,reward,teamCount,userHasEntered,userRank
https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/example-comp,2026-08-01 00:00:00,Playground,Swag,1200,True,784
```

Also update `docs/competitions.md` and `skills/references/competitions.md`, and add a unit test with a mocked `list_competitions` response that includes `user_rank`.

When `userHasEntered` is `True` but `userRank` is `0`, the CLI can print `0` as-is. Docs should note that this can mean no public leaderboard position yet.

## Related

- #66: earlier guidance was to download the full leaderboard and search locally.

## Contribution

Happy to open a PR for this if the approach looks good. Let me know if you have any questions.
title: Expose userRank in kaggle competitions list output

## Objective

Add the base competition catalog model to `sports-catalog-service`.

The goal is to start expanding the catalog beyond sports by introducing competitions linked to an existing sport.

This feature should provide the minimum useful competition functionality without adding seasons, teams, matches or advanced rules yet.

## Context

`sports-catalog-service` currently manages the sports catalog.

The sports functionality already provides the base needed to create, update, list, filter and retrieve sports.

The next natural step is to introduce competitions as catalog entities.

A competition belongs to a sport. For example:

* Football → LaLiga
* Football → Copa del Rey
* Basketball → NBA
* Tennis → Wimbledon

This feature should follow the same architecture already used for sports:

REST Controller
→ CommandBus / QueryBus
→ CommandHandler / QueryHandler
→ Domain model
→ RepositoryPort
→ Persistence adapter

## Functional scope

Introduce a new `Competition` catalog entity.

Initial competition fields:

* `id`
* `sportId`
* `name`
* `type`
* `active`

Initial competition types:

* `LEAGUE`
* `CUP`
* `SUPER_CUP`

Add support for the following operations:

* Create a competition.
* Update a competition name and type.
* List competitions.
* Get competition by id.
* Get competition by name.
* Activate a competition.
* Deactivate a competition.

## Expected endpoints

Create competition:

POST /competitions

Update competition:

PUT /competitions/{id}

List competitions:

GET /competitions

Get competition by id:

GET /competitions/{id}

Get competition by name:

GET /competitions/by-name/{name}

Activate competition:

PATCH /competitions/{id}/activate

Deactivate competition:

PATCH /competitions/{id}/deactivate

## Expected behavior

* A competition must belong to an existing sport.
* A competition name is required.
* A competition type is required.
* A competition is active by default when created.
* A competition can be activated.
* A competition can be deactivated.
* Retrieving a non-existing competition must return the current not found behavior.
* Creating a competition for a non-existing sport must return a controlled error.
* Existing sports functionality must remain unchanged.

## Domain behavior

Create a `Competition` domain model.

The domain model should own the basic rules for competitions:

* `id` is required.
* `sportId` is required.
* `name` is required and cannot be blank.
* `name` should be trimmed.
* `type` is required.
* `active` is controlled through domain behavior.

Expected domain behavior:

* `create(...)`
* `reconstitute(...)`
* `rename(...)`
* `changeType(...)`
* `activate()`
* `deactivate()`

The exact method names can be adjusted if a cleaner domain model emerges during implementation.

## CQRS scope

This feature must follow the existing CQRS structure.

Command side:

* `CreateCompetitionCommand`
* `CreateCompetitionCommandHandler`
* `UpdateCompetitionCommand`
* `UpdateCompetitionCommandHandler`
* `ActivateCompetitionCommand`
* `ActivateCompetitionCommandHandler`
* `DeactivateCompetitionCommand`
* `DeactivateCompetitionCommandHandler`

Query side:

* `ListCompetitionsQuery`
* `ListCompetitionsQueryHandler`
* `GetCompetitionByIdQuery`
* `GetCompetitionByIdQueryHandler`
* `GetCompetitionByNameQuery`
* `GetCompetitionByNameQueryHandler`

Application output:

* Add a `CompetitionResult` application output model.

REST output:

* Add a `CompetitionResponse` REST response model.

## Persistence scope

Add persistence support for competitions.

Expected persistence components:

* `CompetitionJpaEntity`
* `CompetitionPersistenceMapper`
* `SpringDataCompetitionJpaRepository`
* `CompetitionJpaAdapter`
* `CompetitionRepositoryPort`

Add a Flyway migration to create the `competitions` table.

Suggested table fields:

* `id`
* `sport_id`
* `name`
* `type`
* `active`

The database should enforce basic integrity:

* `id` as primary key.
* `sport_id` as required.
* `name` as required.
* `type` as required.
* `active` as required.

Competition name uniqueness should be defined carefully.

Recommended initial rule:

* Competition names should be unique per sport, case-insensitively.

For example:

* Football + LaLiga is valid.
* Basketball + LaLiga could be valid if needed.
* Football + LaLiga and Football + laliga should not both exist.

## Out of scope

* Competition seasons.
* Teams.
* Matches.
* Standings.
* Tournament formats.
* Country or region association.
* External provider ids.
* Translations.
* Aliases.
* Complex competition hierarchy.
* Playoff/subcompetition modeling.
* Pagination and sorting unless already implemented generically and easy to reuse.
* Advanced filtering.
* Event sourcing.
* Messaging.
* Async processing.
* Separate read database.
* Cache.

## Architectural rules

* Competition must follow the existing hexagonal architecture.
* Competition commands must modify state.
* Competition queries must only read state.
* REST controllers must use `CommandBus` and `QueryBus`.
* Command handlers must contain application orchestration only.
* Query handlers must remain read-only.
* Domain models must contain business rules and invariants.
* Domain must not depend on Spring, JPA, REST or CQRS infrastructure.
* Persistence must go through repository ports.
* JPA entities must remain inside infrastructure output persistence.
* REST request and response DTOs must remain inside infrastructure input REST.
* Application output must use `CompetitionResult`.
* JPA entities must not leak into application or domain.
* Existing sports functionality must not be broken.

## Definition of Done

* `Competition` domain model exists.
* Competition type enum exists with `LEAGUE`, `CUP` and `SUPER_CUP`.
* Competition domain invariants are enforced.
* `CompetitionRepositoryPort` exists.
* Competition command classes exist.
* Competition command handlers exist.
* Competition query classes exist.
* Competition query handlers exist.
* `CompetitionResult` exists.
* REST request models for competition operations exist.
* `CompetitionResponse` exists.
* Competition REST controller exists.
* `POST /competitions` is available.
* `PUT /competitions/{id}` is available.
* `GET /competitions` is available.
* `GET /competitions/{id}` is available.
* `GET /competitions/by-name/{name}` is available.
* `PATCH /competitions/{id}/activate` is available.
* `PATCH /competitions/{id}/deactivate` is available.
* A competition can only be created for an existing sport.
* Not found behavior is handled for missing competitions.
* Not found behavior is handled for missing sports when creating a competition.
* Flyway migration creates the `competitions` table.
* Persistence adapter maps between domain and JPA correctly.
* Existing sports functionality continues working.
* The implementation follows the current CQRS structure.
* The implementation follows the current hexagonal architecture.
* The project builds successfully with Maven.
* Existing tests pass.

## Summary

GlideComp scores individual tasks; there is no competition-level (series) ranking. The spec's task/competition ranking sections (S7F §13–14, with definitions in Section 7A) and the FTV (Fixed Total Validity) discard mechanism commonly used in paragliding series are not implemented.

Listed as "Not implemented" on the `/scoring/gap` explainer feature-status table after the spec comparison in #253.

## What the spec says

S7F §13 Task ranking / §14 Competition ranking defer to Section 7A (§5.2.4, §5.2.5): overall, female, and nation rankings, plus tie handling, at both task and competition level.

Competition scoring conventions from S7A / common practice:

- **Sum of task scores** — the simple default: a pilot's competition score is the sum of their task scores.
- **FTV (Fixed Total Validity)** — used in many PG leagues and Cat 1 events: each pilot counts only their best results up to a fixed fraction (typically 25–30% of total validity is discarded), scoring `score/validity`-weighted best tasks. Parameters: FTV percentage, and the per-task validity values already computed by the engine.
- Nation/female sub-rankings filter the same task scores by pilot attributes.

## What GlideComp does today

- Per-task scores only (`web/workers/competition-api/src/scoring.ts`, scores pages). Task validity (needed for FTV weighting) is already computed and stored per task — the engine side is ready.
- No comp-level standings table/route/UI; no discard logic; no nation/female sub-rankings.

## What to implement

1. Competition-standings computation: sum-of-tasks first (covers HG comps and simple series), keyed by `comp_pilot` per class.
2. FTV as a competition `scoring` option with the FTV percentage as a parameter — changes to it must be audit-logged (it changes final standings).
3. Ties per S7A; optional female/nation sub-rankings when pilot metadata exists.
4. A standings page in the SPA (per class), linked from the comp detail page.

## Transparency checklist (part of "done")

- [ ] Update the `/scoring/gap` explainer (`web/frontend/static/src/pages/scoring/gap.astro`): feature-status table rows "Multi-task series scoring" and "FTV", plus a pilot-facing section explaining how series totals (and FTV discards) work.
- [ ] Add a standings explainer analogous to the per-track score analysis: for each pilot, show which tasks counted, which were discarded under FTV, and the arithmetic (`web/engine/src/score-explanation.ts` pattern; surface in the React UI alongside `PilotScoreDetail.tsx`).
- [ ] Update relevant docs under `docs/` (e.g. `docs/competition-spec.md`, `docs/competition-requirements.md`).
- [ ] Audit-log the series-scoring settings (FTV on/off, percentage) via `audit()` per CLAUDE.md.
title: GAP spec: multi-task series scoring and FTV (S7F §13–14, S7A)

This issue tracks correctness, evaluation-rigor, and competition-alignment fixes identified during an internal audit of the pipeline against the Cleveland Clinic "Unlocking undruggable targets" 2026 challenge requirements. Each item links to a follow-up PR when addressed.

## 🔴 Critical — result validity

- [ ] **Test-set leakage in evaluation.** `eval_dual_enaqt.py` and `eval_bce_enaqt_combo.py` grid-search the ENAQT dephasing rate `γ` (and the blend weight `α`) by maximizing `hit_at_k(...)` **against the test protein's ground-truth labels**; `train_hybrid.py` selects the checkpoint by `test_hit` on the 3 challenge proteins. The reported `Avg Hit@5 = 1.000` is therefore **not a blind prediction** and overstates generalization. Fix: held-out validation / nested CV; fix all hyperparameters a priori; touch holo only once.
- [ ] **Wrong validation structure for Cardiac Myosin.** `dataset.py` maps Cardiac Myosin holo to **6C1H**, which RCSB lists as *"High-Resolution Cryo-EM Structures of Actin-bound Myosin States"* = **rat unconventional myosin-Ib + rabbit actin + calmodulin, ligands ADP/MG only, no mavacamten** — a different protein and the orthosteric (ADP) site. Fix: use **9GZ1** (human β-cardiac myosin MYH7 + mavacamten, ligand **XB2**; cryo-EM 3.7 Å) or 8QYQ/8QYR. Ref: https://www.rcsb.org/structure/6C1H , https://www.rcsb.org/structure/9GZ1
- [ ] **The "quantum" winning method is effectively classical.** `enaqt_rwr` is a column-normalized **random-walk-with-restart** `p = α·p₀ + (1−α)·W·p` — a classical Markov process on a (quantum-inspired) rate matrix; coherence/interference is discarded in the Haken–Strobl rate reduction. The genuinely-unitary CTQW path (`ctqw_torch.py`) underperformed. Fix: either label honestly as quantum-inspired, or move to a real finite-time CTQW.

## 🟠 README scientific-claim corrections

- [ ] **"Myristoyl pocket >30 Å with no path in the 12 Å Cα graph, bridged by quantum tunneling" is physically incorrect.** The myristoyl and ATP sites are both in one compact, connected kinase domain, **~25 Å** apart and allosterically coupled (HX-MS: Iacob & Engen, PLOS One 2011, https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0015929 ). For a contact-graph Hamiltonian, `e^{−iHt}` is block-diagonal across disconnected components → zero amplitude transfer; a CTQW cannot "tunnel" across a true graph disconnection. The observed RWR=0.00 is more consistent with a graph-construction artifact (split chains / missing residues) and RWR restart-locality than with a real disconnection.
- [ ] **Mislabeled "apo" structures.** `1OPL` is the autoinhibited multidomain c-Abl carrying an ATP-site inhibitor (P16) **and** the myristoyl group — not apo; `4OBE` is GDP-bound (drug-apo, but carries the nucleotide). Correct the wording.

## 🟡 Evaluation rigor

- [ ] **Hit@5 @ 8 Å is lenient.** Field conventions use 4–5 Å residue membership, Top-1/Top-3, and AUPRC / Jaccard (AlloBench, PASSer, PocketMiner). Internal GT-cutoff sensitivity already shows KRAS drops to ~chance at 4.5 Å (permutation p ≈ 0.86). Fix: report 4.5 Å, Top-1/3/5, AUPRC, permutation significance, and enrichment **with confidence intervals** (enrichment is unstable at tiny base rates).

## 🔵 Competition-requirement gaps (roadmap)

- [ ] No actual quantum circuit / near-term-hardware path (AWS Braket / Classiq), no noise-resilience study, no coarse-graining.
- [ ] The required N×N quantum connectivity matrix from the T→∞ time-average is ≈ 1/N (uninformative for delocalized eigenvectors). Fix: finite-time CTQW / P(j, t*); add Kron reduction (with spectral-interlacing proof) for large targets; add a Trotterized `e^{−iHt}` demo with ⌈log₂N⌉ amplitude encoding; add an ENAQT/Lindblad dephasing scan as the noise-resilience argument.

## Product idea
Build a separate organizer side of the app with a Free and Pro offering.

The organizer product should start by helping clubs publish competition target setups that shooters can find and reuse, and later grow into a full tablet-based competition workflow with live scoring.

## Why this matters
- organizers can create the source setup once instead of every shooter entering the same targets
- shooters can search for the competition and review/confirm the published setup
- shared competition data improves the quality of personal miss analysis and coach reports
- the organizer product can become a separate revenue stream from individual shooter subscriptions
- in Norway it should initially complement established systems such as Leirdue.net rather than try to replace them
- in countries without a dominant national scoring platform, the live competition workflow may have stronger standalone value

## Suggested Free organizer tier
- create an organizer/club profile
- create a competition
- build target/course templates for supported disciplines
- enter target letters, pair type, direction, speed, distance, difficulty and notes where relevant
- publish a searchable competition setup
- allow shooters to find, preview and copy the setup into their own result/session after review
- edit or withdraw a published setup
- basic limits may apply to active events, saved templates or publishing history

The Free tier should create useful shared content and encourage clubs and shooters to join the same ecosystem.

## Suggested Pro organizer tier
- broader discipline-correct setup tools and FITASC programme workflow where permitted
- reusable course and competition libraries
- tablet-optimized scorer interface
- station/stand assignment
- squads, shooters and shooting order
- live hit/miss or score registration during the competition
- multi-device synchronization
- offline-first operation with safe sync when coverage returns
- clear device and sync status
- duplicate/conflict protection
- live leaderboard and progress view
- roles and permissions for organizer, scorer, referee and read-only display
- corrections with an audit log
- exports and integrations for established result systems where possible
- post-event handoff so each shooter can claim or import their own result and add personal miss reasons

## Commercial direction
Prefer an organizer, event or club subscription rather than requiring every scorer to buy an individual Pro account. The paid value should primarily be operational workflow, reliability, synchronization and event management.

Do not make access to public rule documents the main paywall. Before including official FITASC programmes, schemas or documents, confirm what can legally be stored, reproduced and redistributed. Pro can instead provide better tools for using supported programme structures and organizer-owned templates.

## Recommended staged delivery
### Stage 1: shared organizer templates
- organizer creates and publishes competition setup
- shooters search, review and reuse it
- no live scoring
- narrow discipline support

### Stage 2: simple event administration
- squads, shooters, stations and score entry
- one organizer device first
- downloadable/exportable results

### Stage 3: Pro live competition operation
- multiple tablets
- offline-first scoring
- synchronization and conflict handling
- live leaderboard
- roles, audit trail and corrections

### Stage 4: international organizer product
- configurable languages and competition formats
- integrations and exports
- club/event billing
- public event pages and spectator views

## Product constraints
- do not build this before the current shooter app, shared setup model, identity matching and offline foundations are stable
- all organizer flows must work in Light and Dark themes
- mobile and tablet UX must be designed separately from the normal shooter UI
- live scoring must not launch without reliable offline behavior, conflict handling, correction history and event recovery
- keep Training and Competition data clearly separated

## Priority
Later roadmap. First implementation should be shared searchable organizer-created competition templates, not a complete replacement for national competition systems.

## Summary

Hosts cannot set or change their competition's cover image themselves. Today the only UI that writes `competitions.cover_image` is the **super-admin** console — `admin/src/features/super-admin/components/CompetitionEditModal.jsx`. There is no cover-upload field anywhere in the host-facing app (`src/`), so a host has to ask a platform admin to set it.

This surfaced while fixing the New York "Most Eligible Bachelorettes" card, which was showing a Chicago skyline because its `cover_image` was never set (and the code fallback was city-blind). The fallback is now city-aware, but hosts still can't upload a branded cover on their own.

## Current behavior (for reference)

- Public card resolves its image via `getCompetitionImage(competition)` → returns `competition.cover_image` first, else falls back to a city/state skyline (`src/utils/cityImages.js`).
- Upload flow that exists today (super-admin only):
  - `handleCoverUpload` validates image + <5MB, uploads to Supabase Storage bucket `competition-images` under `covers/<timestamp>-<rand>.<ext>`, stores the public URL in `cover_image` (`CompetitionEditModal.jsx:104`).
  - Persisted on save via `CompetitionsManager.jsx:507` (`cover_image: formData.cover_image || null`).

## Proposed work

- Add a cover-image upload field to the host-facing competition setup (likely `SetupTab`), reusing the same `competition-images` bucket + `covers/` path convention and the same validation (image type, <5MB).
- Save to `competitions.cover_image`.
- Confirm Supabase Storage RLS / policies allow a host (not just service role / super-admin) to upload to `competition-images` and update their own competition's `cover_image`.
- Show a preview + Replace/Remove actions, matching the existing admin modal UX.

## Notes / open questions

- Decide whether hosts can edit the cover at any phase or only before publish.
- Consider normalizing/resizing on upload (relates to the logo-normalization work in #598).

Priority: low — deferred, do later.
title: [host UI] Self-serve competition cover-image upload (host-facing, not just super-admin)
